what_it_does: When engineers simulate a circuit over time and want to know how sensitive the circuit's output is to each of its internal parameters (for example, to tune the design), a mathematical technique called adjoint sensitivity analysis can compute all those sensitivities efficiently in one reverse pass. The catch is that this reverse pass must look back at every saved snapshot of the circuit's state from every previous time step, which requires storing an enormous amount of data — often more than fits in memory for large circuits or long simulations. MemSens addresses this by compressing those stored snapshots using a 'lossy' scheme (one that throws away some detail on purpose) while guaranteeing that the errors introduced stay within strict, user-specified bounds. The compression exploits the fact that circuit states tend to change smoothly across time and space, allowing high compression ratios without ruining the accuracy of the final sensitivity numbers.
